newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GE's Hungary bank unit, BB boosts H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: GE's Hungary bank unit, BB boosts H1 profits.

text.p: Hungary's Budapest Bank (BB) posted 3.5 billion forint pre-tax profits in the first half of this year, the same amount as in the whole of 1995, the bank said in a statement on Thursday.

General Electric Capital Services, a member of the U.S. GE group and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) holds a joint majority stake in BB since the bank's privatisation in last December.

Profitability was improved by higher operating profits and a firmer grip on lending rules, the bank said, adding that the amount of loan loss provisions it made in the first half of this year was only quarter of that of whole 1995.
Increasing its activity on the interbank market and securities buying, BB has boosted its lending by four percent in the first half of this year, which also led to the better results, the bank said.
BB's assets amounted to 212.5 billion forints at the end of June, compared with 212.9 billion forints at the end of 1995.
Despite the decrease in real assets, the bank has preserved its market share, six percent of the total banking assets in Hungary, BB added.
BB increased the number of its clients by 50,000 to almost 340,000 in the January-June period, the bank said.
